established_findings.statement: LLMs are being actively integrated into intent-driven NetOps workflows (intent→configuration, multi-agent orchestration) in both research and production-facing projects.
limitations: Reports range from academic prototypes to company-run frameworks; details of production deployment and scale vary across sources.
Some projects emphasize architecture and integration rather than broad public benchmarks of operational outcomes.

established_findings.statement: Hallucination, overconfidence, and miscalibrated uncertainty in LLM outputs are well-documented and relevant risks for NetOps tasks that require deterministic correctness.
established_findings.evidence_type: surveys and empirical studies on hallucination/uncertainty
limitations: Most analyses are cross-domain; NetOps-specific calibration studies remain fewer in number.
Calibration improvements are reported but do not eliminate all failure modes in high-stakes action-execution pipelines.

established_findings.statement: Guarded architectures that combine generation with deterministic verification/validation (generate→verify→repair) materially improve reliability for LLM-driven network actions.
limitations: Improvements are task- and validator-dependent; verification tools have scalability and fidelity trade-offs.
Comparisons are often against unconstrained baselines rather than a comprehensive set of mitigations.

established_findings.statement: Action-level risks exist: false or misleading model claims can trigger downstream tool calls or concrete actions at high rates unless mitigations are applied.
limitations: The Claim-to-Action experiments are controlled and sandboxed; real-world operational contexts may introduce different rates but the core failure mode is demonstrated.
Mitigation effectiveness depends on exact agent/tool integration and policy phrasing.

established_findings.statement: Network verification and formal-analysis tools (e.g., Batfish, Plankton, ACORN) provide high-fidelity checks that are central to safe deployment of generated configurations, but they entail scalability and protocol-coverage trade-offs.
limitations: Tool performance and protocol support vary; some verification techniques require heavy engineering for industrial topologies.
Integration between LLM outputs and formal verifiers is not universally automated in existing literature.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent can LLM-generated network configurations be integrated into formal verification pipelines at Internet-scale topologies without impractical engineering effort?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: verification tool papers (showing capabilities and limits)
limitations: Existing verification papers demonstrate scale improvements but do not fully characterize end-to-end LLM→verify deployments at operational ISP/enterprise scales.
Practical integration effort estimates are not standardized across studies.

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably can LLM uncertainty proxies (verbalized confidence, sampling consistency, other black-box methods) predict concrete action-safety for NetOps tasks in production?
limitations: Most uncertainty studies focus on QA/reasoning tasks or medical benchmarks rather than direct tool-call safety in NetOps.
Transferring proxy performance to action-safety requires task-specific validation.

unresolved_questions.statement: What are the realistic failure rates and root causes when agentic LLMs execute network-change workflows under adversarial or ambiguous operator intents?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: red-team/attack-framework experiments and adversarial prompt literature
limitations: Existing red-team experiments show high vulnerability in many domains but NetOps-specific adversarial campaign studies remain limited.
Failure rates depend strongly on agent design, tool scoping, and human oversight processes.

unresolved_questions.statement: How representative are common NetOps benchmarks and synthetic datasets of real operator intents, topology diversity, and failure modes?
limitations: Several benchmark efforts exist, but systematic ecological-validity comparisons against production telemetry are sparse in supplied records.
Some datasets/prototypes are promising but limited in protocol/vendor/scale coverage.

unresolved_questions.statement: Can human-in-the-loop oversight, as typically implemented, reliably prevent high-impact automated NetOps errors, or does oversight often function as a procedural 'ceremony' under time pressure?
limitations: Empirical studies of human oversight in NetOps context are limited; governance/critique sources highlight conceptual risks but not comprehensive operator-in-the-loop field studies.
Effectiveness likely depends on UI, operator training, and procedural design.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a gap in executable, action-level NetOps benchmarks that deterministically evaluate whether an LLM-driven pipeline causes correct/incorrect tool actions (not just text correctness).
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: executable-benchmark concept papers and claim-to-action experiments
limitations: PROBE (chemistry) demonstrates the executable benchmark concept outside networking; direct NetOps equivalents are less mature in the supplied records.
NetConfEval and Claim-to-Action show partial steps but no widely adopted standard executable NetOps benchmark yet.

candidate_gaps.statement: Public, diverse corpora of real-world network device configurations and operator intent traces suitable for LLM training/evaluation remain limited or non-uniformly available.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: benchmark & tool literature noting dataset needs
limitations: Some datasets and corpora exist in research but coverage (vendor commands, enterprise topologies, intent logs) is inconsistent across sources.
Privacy and operational sensitivity constrain public release of many real configs.

candidate_gaps.statement: Comparative evaluations of mitigation architectures (e.g., RAG + verifier + human-approval vs. strict proof-constrained action) specific to NetOps are sparse.
limitations: Proposals and early system reports exist, but systematic head-to-head empirical comparisons in NetOps settings are limited in the supplied corpus.
Different proposals assume different threat models and operational constraints, complicating direct comparison.

candidate_gaps.statement: Tooling to reliably detect and mitigate adversarial prompt attacks specifically targeted at NetOps agent pipelines needs further development and standardized evaluation.
limitations: Existing mitigation engines and scanners are evaluated in general LLM contexts; NetOps-specific attack taxonomies and benchmarks are underdeveloped in the supplied records.
Scanner reliability varies and benchmark datasets for attacks are nascent.

candidate_gaps.statement: Operational metrics and scoring protocols for agentic NetOps (trace quality, bounded tool use, replayable sandbox scoring, rollback-aware scoring) are incompletely standardized.
limitations: Papers argue for workflow-centred evaluation but do not converge on a single standard metric set in the supplied literature.
Implementation of proposed evaluation regimes varies by organization and research group.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is limited published evidence quantifying how much human oversight reduces real-world operational harms for LLM-driven NetOps versus automated verification approaches.
limitations: Governance critique highlights conceptual weaknesses but lacks large-scale NetOps field studies measuring mitigation effect sizes.
System reports describe human-in-the-loop designs but often lack controlled comparisons isolating human oversight benefit.

excluded_claims: LLMs by themselves (without verification/tooling) are sufficiently reliable for unsupervised production deployment of network configuration changes.

Any single cited system is proven to be 'production-ready' across all enterprise/ISP environments; supplied records show prototypes, frameworks, or company reports but not universal production validation.
There is conclusive evidence that human oversight, as commonly implemented, reliably prevents high-impact agentic NetOps failures in all operational contexts.
A standardized, widely adopted executable NetOps benchmark that deterministically scores action-level correctness already exists and is broadly used.
Claims of absolute provable zero-risk agentic deployment in NetOps (i.e., formal guarantees that eliminate all attack success) are not supported by the supplied records.
